lexicon.aiaas: Rent AI capability instead of raising your own.
lexicon.api: The window through which two systems talk to each other.
lexicon.api-key: The password string used to connect — it decides whose bill it lands on.
lexicon.adoption: Turning a tool into something people actually use every day.
lexicon.agent: An AI that doesn't just answer — it plans the steps and finishes the whole job itself.
lexicon.agent-loop: The cycle where the AI takes a step, checks the result, then decides the next one.
lexicon.alignment: Getting the AI to behave the way people want it to.
lexicon.anomaly-detection: Picking the few odd entries out of a pile of normal ones.
lexicon.automation-tool: Wiring different services together by drag and drop, no code.
lexicon.benchmark: A standard set of questions for testing models, giving a score you can compare.
lexicon.black-box: It gave an answer, but nobody can say why it answered that way.
lexicon.blind-spot: The things you don't know you've missed.

lexicon.claude-md: Write the rules once; they take effect automatically every time you start work.
lexicon.chain-of-thought: Have it write out its reasoning — the answer gets more accurate.
lexicon.chatgpt: The product that brought AI chat into public view.
lexicon.citation: A link or passage the AI attaches saying where a sentence came from.
lexicon.citizen-developer: An employee who isn't an engineer but builds tools to solve problems anyway.
lexicon.claude: Another company's AI assistant, well regarded for long text and code.
lexicon.claude-code: An AI assistant that runs in the terminal and can touch your files directly.
lexicon.clustering: Let the machine sort data into piles, then you look at what the piles are.
lexicon.context: Everything it can see in front of it during this one conversation.
lexicon.context-engineering: Managing what material it gets to see this time, not just how you ask.
lexicon.context-window: The ceiling on how much one conversation can hold.
lexicon.copilot: Microsoft's umbrella name for the AI features hung on its own products.
lexicon.copyright: Who owns what the AI made, and whether it can be used commercially.
lexicon.cursor: A code editor with AI integrated deep inside.
lexicon.data-cleaning: Tidying up typos, duplicates, gaps and inconsistent formats in data.
lexicon.data-drift: The world changed, but the model is still stuck at the moment it was trained.
lexicon.data-labeling: People tag data one item at a time with what it is, so the AI can learn.
lexicon.data-retention: How long the other side keeps what you put in, and whether it gets used for training.
lexicon.decision-tree: A chain of yes-or-no questions; follow it to the end and you get the answer.
lexicon.deep-learning: One approach in machine learning: many stacked layers handling complex things.
lexicon.deepfake: AI-made faces, voices or videos convincing enough to pass as real.
lexicon.acceptance-checklist: The completion criteria you check line by line before accepting delivery.
lexicon.design-token: Name the colours, type sizes and spacing first; afterwards refer to names, not values.
lexicon.differential-privacy: Add a little noise to the data so the overall statistics stay accurate but no individual can be identified.
lexicon.diffusion: The mainstream way AI generates images — 'washing' a picture out of a blob of noise, step by step.
lexicon.discriminative-ai: The kind of AI that only judges, never produces.
lexicon.division-of-labor: Decide what to keep for your own judgement; hand over the rest.
lexicon.domain-skill: Write down an industry's insider rules so the AI can judge by them.
lexicon.embedding: Convert a piece of text into a set of coordinates; similar meanings land close together.
lexicon.expert-system: Write an expert's judgement as a list of rules and let the computer follow them.
lexicon.explainable-ai: Finding ways to make an AI's judgements understandable — and challengeable — by people.
lexicon.give-example: Show it an old piece of work you were happy with; it beats three paragraphs of description.
lexicon.fine-tuning: Take a model that already knows things and teach it a batch of your own, so it fits your usage better.
lexicon.gan: Two AIs sparring — one forges, one catches forgeries, and both get stronger.
lexicon.gemini: Google's AI assistant, tied fairly tightly to its own services.
lexicon.generative-ai: AI that produces new things, not just classifies or predicts.
lexicon.graph-engineering: Instead of letting the AI run step by step to the end, draw the map of which situation takes which path first.
lexicon.grill-me: Before you start, have the AI turn around and ask you the questions.
lexicon.grounding: Require every claim the AI makes to point back to a real piece of data.
lexicon.guardrail: Turn 'the things that absolutely must not go wrong' into checks that block automatically.
lexicon.hallucination: The AI states, in a very confident tone, something that doesn't exist.
lexicon.harness: The whole layer wrapped around the AI — what it can touch, what stops it, how it's checked.
lexicon.harness-engineering: Put the effort into designing the AI's working environment, not into how you phrase the request.
lexicon.human-in-the-loop: The process runs automatically, but at certain points a person must click confirm.
lexicon.independent-review: The person who did the work doesn't check it; bring in someone who wasn't involved.
lexicon.inference: The act of the model actually running once and producing an answer.
lexicon.iteration: Don't aim to nail it in one go; make a rough version and improve it round by round.
lexicon.jailbreak: Talking your way around the AI's limits so it says things it normally wouldn't.
lexicon.knowledge-cutoff: Its knowledge stops on a certain day; it doesn't know anything after that.
lexicon.llm: A system that, having read an enormous amount of text, learned to 'continue the next sentence'.
lexicon.liability: When the AI says something wrong and causes a loss, who is responsible.
lexicon.license-terms: The rules for what you may and may not do with this thing.
lexicon.local-inference: The AI runs on your own computer or server; the data never leaves.
lexicon.loop-engineering: Designing how the AI's self-running cycle runs, and when it stops.
lexicon.mcp: Lets the AI reach your inbox, calendar and files — not just chat.
lexicon.machine-learning: Instead of hard-coding rules, give it lots of examples and let it find the patterns.
lexicon.maintainability: When someone has to change it six months from now, do they have to learn it all over again?
lexicon.memory: Lets the AI remember you across conversations, so you don't reintroduce yourself every time.
lexicon.midjourney: An AI image service known for its aesthetics.
lexicon.model: The AI's 'brain' itself — separate from the interface you use.
lexicon.model-collapse: When AI keeps learning from AI-generated content, quality degrades round after round.
lexicon.multimodal: The ability to understand images and sound, not just text.
lexicon.no-code: Tools that let you build things by dragging or configuring, without writing code.
lexicon.notebooklm: An AI notebook that answers only from the documents you uploaded.
lexicon.ocr: Turn the text in an image or scan into text you can copy and search.
lexicon.private-deployment: Install the whole AI stack on your own machines; data never leaves your environment.
lexicon.open-source-model: A model you can download and run yourself, as opposed to only connecting to someone else's.
lexicon.outlier: The few entries that are clearly unlike the rest of the data.
lexicon.output-style: Set once how it talks to you; every reply follows from then on.
lexicon.overfitting: Memorised the past exam papers perfectly, then can't handle a new one.
lexicon.poc: Build something small first to prove the path works, then decide whether to invest.
lexicon.parameter-count: A number for model size, usually written like 7B or 70B.
lexicon.perplexity: An AI service whose main pitch is search plus answers with sources attached.
lexicon.persona-setting: Tell it who it is now before telling it what to do.
lexicon.plan-mode: Have it list what it intends to do first; it only acts after you nod.
lexicon.prompt: What you say to the AI.
lexicon.prompt-engineering: Treating 'how to phrase it so it does it right' as a craft you can practise.
lexicon.prompt-injection: Hiding commands inside data so the AI mistakes them for your instructions.
lexicon.prompt-template: Save the phrasing that worked; paste it next time and go.
lexicon.quantization: Shrink the model a little in exchange for it running at all, and faster.
lexicon.rag: Before the AI answers, have it go through the pile of material you specified.
lexicon.rlhf: Keep having people rate the AI's answers, tuning it toward what people prefer.
lexicon.roi: Which is bigger: what you spent, or what you saved.
lexicon.reasoning-model: The kind of model that takes time to think a round before answering.
lexicon.reinforcement-learning: Let it keep trying, reward it when it gets things right, and it gradually learns what works best.
lexicon.risk-matrix: Rank risks by 'how often it happens' times 'how bad it is when it does'.
lexicon.sla: The contract states how long an outage counts as a breach, and how much they pay you.
lexicon.saas: Software isn't installed on your computer; open a browser, log in, and use it.
lexicon.scheduled-run: Have it run by itself on a schedule; you just check the results in the morning.
lexicon.semantic-search: Search for meaning, not words — it finds things even when the wording differs.
lexicon.skill: Package a whole procedure into one command; call it and it runs.
lexicon.source-of-truth: One place has the final say on a thing; everywhere else is its shadow.
lexicon.spec-driven: Write down clearly what it should become first, then let the AI build.
lexicon.speech-to-text: Turn a recording into a transcript.
lexicon.structured-data: Data neatly arranged in a table, as opposed to scattered across documents, emails and photos.
lexicon.subagent: A stand-in you can dispatch: hand it a slice of work, or have it verify independently.
lexicon.subscription: A fixed monthly fee, usually per head.
lexicon.supervised-learning: Give it a pile of 'question plus correct answer' and let it learn how to answer.
lexicon.synthetic-data: Fake data generated by AI, used for training or testing.
lexicon.system-prompt: The setup the user never sees, but which is in effect for every line of the conversation.
lexicon.tco: Every cost from purchase to disposal, not just the purchase price.
lexicon.technical-debt: Take the makeshift route to go fast; later you pay it back with interest.
lexicon.temperature: The knob that controls whether it answers conservatively or lets its imagination run.
lexicon.text-to-speech: Read text aloud, in a voice you can choose.
lexicon.token: The AI's billing unit, roughly 'a small chunk of text'.
lexicon.training: The one-off process where a model reads a huge amount of data and forms its abilities.
lexicon.transformer: The underlying design almost every mainstream AI model shares today.
lexicon.unsupervised-learning: Give it no answers; let it find the patterns in the data by itself.
lexicon.usage-based-pricing: Pay for what you use — no monthly fee, no ceiling.
lexicon.vector-database: A database built specifically for finding content with similar meaning.
lexicon.vendor-lockin: After using it long enough you can't switch, because moving costs too much.
lexicon.vibe-coding: Don't look at the code; just state what you need and let the AI keep going.
lexicon.watermark: Hide a mark inside AI-generated content to prove a machine made it.
lexicon.personal-data-law: When handling data that can identify a person, the law has a set of requirements.
lexicon.multi-version: Ask for three versions at once; choose, don't revise.
